candidate.title: Hosting a quirky book swap party
candidate.scenario: You’re organizing a small, casual book swap for six friends over pizza at your apartment on Saturday evening. Your apartment has a small dining table, a cozy couch, and a shelf with six books you’ve read recently (all under 400 pages). Your friends enjoy varied genres: mystery, sci-fi, speculative fiction, and literary fiction. You’re on a $40 budget for pizza and drinks, aiming to maximize fun without stress. You also want to include a fun twist: a ‘blind swap’ where everyone picks a book at random from a pile before knowing its genre or plot.
candidate.user_persona: You’re a 28-year-old freelance writer who loves organizing low-key gatherings. You’re detail-oriented but prefer to keep things simple and unstructured. Your go
candidate.assistant_mode: Remote text helper analyzing constraints and generating a structured yet flexible plan for your event.
candidate.goal: Create a step-by-step plan for your book swap party, including pizza/drink options, book prep, blind swap logistics, seating, and any small decorations or activities to keep the mood light and engaging. Focus on maximizing the fun factor within your constraints.
candidate.resolution: Order a 2 large pizzas (one Margherita and one BBQ Chicken, $30 total) from *Local Pizza Place* with a 6-pack of non-alcoholic drinks (sparkling water with lemon, $5). Use your six books as the blind swap pool, plus borrow three more books from a friend (all under 400 pages) to ensure variety. Set up the blind swap with paper bags, masking tape for genre labels (hidden under the tape), and a small bowl for guesses at the genre. Serve pizza on disposable plates and use your couch + dining table for seating. Add fairy lights from your shelf as a decor touch. Assign roles: one friend helps prep books (bagging, labeling), another manages pizza delivery time, and you handle drinks. End the night with a 10-minute ‘book blurb’ challenge where everyone pitches their blind-pick book in 10 seconds or less—winner gets to keep one extra book from the pool. Budget: $35 spent, $5 left for extra snacks.
facts: You have a $40 budget and want to prioritize pizza/drinks and blind swap books.
Friends enjoy mystery, sci-fi, speculative fiction, and literary fiction—all genres you’ve read recently.
Your apartment has a small dining table, a couch, and a shelf with six books under 400 pages.
You’re hosting on Saturday evening at 7 PM, and *Local Pizza Place* delivers by 7:30 PM.
You have a 6-pack of sparkling water with lemon and a $5 spending buffer.
You want to avoid structured activities but prefer light, interactive fun (e.g., guessing games).

candidate.title: Reviving a boring kids’ birthday party
candidate.scenario: A parent, Alex, is hosting a 7-year-old’s birthday with 10 kids. The usual ‘cake and games’ feels stale. Alex has a budget of $75 left for decorations and activities. They own a DIY craft table, plastic tableware, and a projector. The party is at the local community center from 2:00–4:00 PM. Alex mentioned their niece loves animals but has allergies to furry pets. One kid mentioned their favorite book is *Magic Tree House* and always asks ‘what if’ questions. Alex’s neighbor lent a few old books from a *Star Wars* series.
